messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing our Android sample app hang on streaming responses after upgrading to SDK 1.4.0 + Retrofit 2.9? Reproducer on Pixel 8 / Android 14.
maria: Steps: start chat stream -> send partial tokens -> app stalls for ~30s then returns 504 from gateway. No obvious exceptions in app logs.
devon: hmm. any okhttp logs? could be connection pool eviction or http2 pings getting weird on Android 14.
maria: attaching log snippet from device: 
```
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/stream
I/OkHttp: <-- 504 Gateway Timeout (ms=30122)
W/OkHttp: ConnectionPool: removing leaked connection
W/AndroidRuntime: Thread-1: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: timeout
```
kai: that "removing leaked connection" usually means calls didn't close response body. But our SDK wraps streams — maybe the cancellation path isn't calling response.close().
sandra: could be related to our retry layer re-issuing requests and duplicating the Authorization header on retries on older okhttp versions? We saw similar on emulator but not on device.
maria: this repros on device only, not on emulator. Pixel 8 with AOSP okhttp backport?
android-oncall: tagging for visibility @android-oncall :eyes: can you triage whether this is Retrofit/OkHttp or SDK layer?
android-oncall: taking a look. quick Q: which CallFactory are you using? Default or custom?
maria: default from our sampleapp, no custom client. SDK init: `RedwoodClient.create(context)`
devon: try replacing client with an explicit OkHttpClient that sets keepAlive and a smaller Dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost as a workaround. On some devices the system HTTP stack aggressively evicts idle connections when the app is backgrounded.
kai: sample snippet that helped me in another repo: 
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // stream indefinitely
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequestsPerHost = 8 })
  .build()
val retrofit = Retrofit.Builder().callFactory(client).baseUrl(BASE).build()
```
devon: also try `new ConnectionSpec.Builder(ConnectionSpec.COMPATIBLE_TLS).build()` if TLS handshake differences are present on Android 14.
maria: added snippet to sample app, still saw occasional stalls but less frequent. stack traces now show retry attempts: 
```
W/SDK-Retry: Retrying request (attempt=2) - duplicate header authorization: Bearer ...
```
sandra: ah that matches the retry layer bug I filed last week — retries append headers instead of replacing when using non-mutable header builder. I'll re-open that PR.
android-oncall: good catch. Two paths here: 1) fix retry header duplication in SDK, 2) harden sample app with explicit OkHttpClient settings and ensure response bodies are closed on cancellation.
maria: quick question: how do we ensure the streaming response body close path is hit on coroutine cancellation? We're using `suspendCancellableCoroutine` around the stream and calling `call.cancel()` in the cancel handler. Is that enough?
kai: call.cancel() should close it, but ensure you're not leaking the Response object reference elsewhere. Also prefer `body.source().close()` in finally block.
devon: FWIW, Retrofit's `awaitResponse()` adapters sometimes swallow cancellation — if using a custom adapter, make sure it forwards cancellation to the Call.
maria: filing a minimal repro repo now (link: https://git.internal/repro/android14-stream-leak). added a tiny emulator/adb script.
build-bot: CI failure on sampleapp: 1 flaky test: StreamIntegrationTest.testPartialTokenStream - timed out after 60s. See: https://ci.redwood/test/12345
sandra: I'm going to land a header-fix patch for retry behavior and add a unit test around header replacement. I'll also add a note in the sample app README about OkHttp settings for Android 14.
maria: thanks. after header fix + client tweaks I will rerun the Pixel 8 repro and update thread.
android-oncall: schedule: I'll queue an on-device lab run for tomorrow morning. tagging @devex for visibility.
kai: long-term we should add an instrumentation test on a Pixel 8 to catch connection pool evictions + streaming regressions across Android releases.
maria: agreed. leaving TODO in tracker: ENG-4521 (add device test + sampleapp default client change).
devon: if anyone hits this and needs a quick workaround, set `callTimeout`+`readTimeout` to 0 and use explicit ConnectionPool in the client. Not a perfect fix but helps.
sandra: PR: https://git.internal/p/sandra/retry-header-fix ready for review.
maria: awesome — will validate once merged. thanks all :tada:
